newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Blue chip shares keep Casablanca bourse afloat.
newsitem.headline: Blue chip shares keep Casablanca bourse afloat.

text.p: The Casablanca bourse ended its two-hour session slightly higher thanks to the market's blue chip shares including ONA Group, brokers said.
The all-share index rose 0.05 percent to 433.36 points.
ONA, Morocco's largest private group, gained two dirhams to close at 472 dirhams.
"There is an increase in demand for blue chips including ONA and Societe Nationale d'Investissement," Sanae Bennouna, a stockbroker at Upline Securities said.
"The bourse index is expected to continue its upward trend due to positive expectations for the largest capitalisation companies," Bennouna said.
Traded volume on the official market was 24.2 million dirhams, compared with 36.8 million, while trading on the over the counter market dropped to 6.2 million dirhams from 56.3 million on Wednesday.
"The difference is due to the large blocks of brewery Brasseries du Maroc and edible oil firm Lesieur shares which exchanged hands on Wednesday," Bennouna said.
SNI, which has stakes in more than 40 companies, closed at 585 dirhams, up five dirhams over Wednesday's session.
Samir oil refinery, the country's main refinery, rose one dirham to close at 251 dirhams.
The government plans to privatise up to 50 percent of its stake in the oil plant by end 1996.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, one of the market's liquid stocks, remained stable at 400 dirhams.
